task.title: Push Commits
task.shortdesc: Send your local commits to the remote repository so others can see them.

info.p: The push is sent to the remote tracked by the current branch. To push to a different remote, use the submenu in the menu or in the menu.

result.p: The Git Client sends your commits to the remote branch. If the branch exists only locally, it creates a matching remote branch and starts tracking it. If the repository has more than one remote, you are prompted to choose which one to publish the branch to.
result.note: To keep two servers in sync with a single push, assign multiple push URLs to one remote with git remote set-url --add --push <remote> <url>. The Git Client pushes by remote name, so one action reaches every URL you added. This is one way to mirror a repository, which is a type of push-to-all-remotes action.
